title: Hereditary discrepancy and factorization norms (AimPL) — Problem 1.2: Beck-Fiala for random set systems

problems.sourceStatement: Each element $i\in [n]$ lies in $t$ randomly selected sets from $\mathcal{S}$. They show that when $m\ge n$, hereditary discrepancy of the set system is $O(\sqrt{t\log t})$ whp. When $n\ge m^t$, hereditary discrepancy is $O(1)$. An open question is to explore this setting for the remaining range of parameters i.e. when $n^{1/t} < m < n$.
problems.problem: Determine the (hereditary) discrepancy of a random $t$-sparse set system: $n$ elements, $m$ sets, each element placed in $t$ sets chosen uniformly at random. Is it $O(\sqrt{t})$ with high probability for all $n, m$ and all $t$, and in particular in the intermediate regime $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$ for small $t$?
problems.wordDescription: A natural test case for the Beck-Fiala conjecture is the random $t$-sparse model in which every element is put into $t$ uniformly random sets. Ezra and Lovett (2015) showed that the hereditary discrepancy is $O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ when $m \geq n$ and $O(1)$ when $n \gg m^t$, leaving open the intermediate regime. Subsequent work essentially settled the discrepancy of the whole system for moderately large $t$: Potukuchi (2018) proved $O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely for $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$, and Bansal and Meka (2019) proved a tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ bound for the entire range of $n$ and $m$ provided $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$. In the related regime of many columns, Franks and Saks showed discrepancy at most $2$ for random $t$-sparse matrices once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$, Hoberg and Rothvoss showed discrepancy at most $1$ for the i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$ model when $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$, and Potukuchi lowered this threshold to $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ for $p = 1/2$. The remaining gaps (very small $t$ in the intermediate range $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$, and the hereditary version of the newer bounds) were closed from the worst-case side in September 2026: Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2) prove $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix of column sparsity $t$, deterministically and for all $n, m$; since column-restrictions remain $t$-sparse, $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ as well. The random model therefore has (hereditary) discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ in every regime. What remains is the exact order in regimes where the truth is $o(\sqrt{t})$ (e.g. $O(1)$ for $n \gg m^t$), and efficient algorithms, since the Guo-Fang-Lu argument is non-constructive.
problems.mathematicalConditions: Model $\mathcal{H}_1(n, m, t)$. Elements $X = [n]$, sets $S_1, \dots, S_m$; independently for each $x \in X$, a uniformly random $t$-subset $T_x \subseteq [m]$ is chosen and $x$ is placed in exactly the sets $S_j$, $j \in T_x$. Let $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ be the incidence matrix. $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \min_{x \in \{-1,1\}^n} \|Ax\|_\infty$; $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = \max_{J \subseteq [n]} \mathrm{disc}(A_J)$ where $A_J$ is the column-restriction to $J$. All statements are 'with high probability' (w.h.p.), i.e. with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $n \to \infty$, with $m = m(n)$ and $t = t(n)$. Question. Is $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m, t$; and is the same true for $\mathrm{herdisc}(A)$? Benchmarks. $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ w.h.p. if $m \geq n$, and $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(1)$ w.h.p. if $n \gg m^t$ (Ezra-Lovett 2015). $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely when $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$ (Potukuchi 2018). $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $n, m$ whenever $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$ (Bansal-Meka 2019, stated as tight: the discrepancy is also $\Omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in the regimes where the sets have size $\gg t$). Many-columns regime of $\mathcal{H}_1$: $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 2$ w.h.p. once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$ (Franks-Saks 2020, improving Ezra-Lovett's $n \geq m^t$). Related model $\mathcal{H}_2(n, m, p)$: the entries of $A \in \{0,1\}^{m \times n}$ are i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$; $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 1$ w.h.p. when $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$ (Hoberg-Rothvoss 2019), and $\mathrm{disc}(A) \leq 1$ a.s. when $p = 1/2$ and $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ (Potukuchi 2018, answering a question of Hoberg-Rothvoss). Complete resolution. A proof that, in $\mathcal{H}_1(n,m,t)$, $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m = m(n)$ and all $1 \leq t \leq m$ (any growth of $t$), together with either the same for $\mathrm{herdisc}(A)$ or a proof that $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = \omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in some regime; or a disproof exhibiting a regime with $\mathrm{disc}(A) = \omega(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. Minimal progress that counts as a solution of this record. Any of: (i) $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for all $m$ and all $t \geq t_0$ with $t_0 = o((\log\log m)^2)$ (e.g. $t_0 = O(1)$ or $t_0 = O(\log\log m)$); (ii) for fixed $t \geq 3$, determining whether $\mathrm{disc}(A) = O(1)$ w.h.p. throughout $n^{1/t} \ll m \ll n$ (or finding a sub-regime where it is not); (iii) $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. for $m \geq n$ (removing the $\sqrt{\log t}$ of Ezra-Lovett) or in any intermediate regime not covered by Ezra-Lovett; (iv) a polynomial-time algorithm finding a coloring of discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ w.h.p. in a regime where only an existential bound is known. Improvements of constants or of the exponent $10$ in $\log^{10} n$ do not count. Resolution (September 2026). Guo-Fang-Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2) give $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix with at most $t$ ones per column, hence for every realization of $\mathcal{H}_1(n, m, t)$ and every column-restriction $A_J$: $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ surely, for all $m$ and all $t$. This meets the complete-resolution criterion (both $\mathrm{disc}$ and $\mathrm{herdisc}$ are $O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $m, t$) and items (i) and (iii); the record is solved. Still open: item (iv) (a polynomial-time algorithm), and the exact order of $\mathrm{disc}(A)$ in regimes where it is $o(\sqrt{t})$.

literature.title: E. Ezra, S. Lovett, On the Beck-Fiala conjecture for random set systems, APPROX/RANDOM 2015; Random Structures & Algorithms 54(4):665-675, 2019
literature.description: Introduces the random $t$-sparse model and proves $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ w.h.p. for $m \geq n$ and $O(1)$ for $n \gg m^t$.

literature.title: A. Potukuchi, Discrepancy in random hypergraph models, arXiv:1811.01491, 2018
literature.description: In the model where every element lies in exactly $t$ random sets, proves discrepancy $O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely when $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$ (improving Ezra-Lovett in this range); in the i.i.d. model with $p = 1/2$ and $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ proves discrepancy at most $1$, answering a question of Hoberg-Rothvoss.

literature.title: N. Bansal, R. Meka, On the discrepancy of random low degree set systems, SODA 2019; Random Structures & Algorithms 57(3):695-705, 2020
literature.description: Proves a tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ discrepancy bound for the random $t$-sparse model for the entire range of $n$ and $m$ under $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$.

literature.title: R. Hoberg, T. Rothvoss, A Fourier-analytic approach for the discrepancy of random set systems, SODA 2019; arXiv:1806.04484
literature.description: Introduces Fourier-analytic discrepancy bounds and applies them to the i.i.d. Bernoulli$(p)$ model: for $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$ the discrepancy is at most $1$ w.h.p. (previously $O(1)$ only for $n \gg m^t$ by Ezra-Lovett); the threshold was lowered to $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ for $p = 1/2$ by Potukuchi.

literature.title: C. Franks, M. Saks, On the discrepancy of random matrices with many columns, Random Structures & Algorithms 57(1):64-96, 2020
literature.description: Local-limit-theorem approach (via Fourier analysis) to the discrepancy of random $m \times n$ matrices with i.i.d. columns. For random $t$-sparse matrices ($t$ ones per column) shows $\ell_\infty$-discrepancy at most $2$ w.h.p. once $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$, improving the $n \geq m^t$ requirement of Ezra-Lovett.

literature.title: S. Guo, E. X. Fang, J. Lu, Vector balancing via directional total variation, arXiv:2609.11189, 2026
literature.description: Corollary 1.2: $\mathrm{disc}(A) < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$ for every $0/1$ matrix with at most $t$ ones per column (the Beck-Fiala conjecture), derived from the Komlós bound $3\sqrt{2\pi}$. Applied to every realization of $\mathcal{H}_1(n,m,t)$ and every column-restriction, it gives $\mathrm{herdisc}(A) = O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $n, m, t$. Existential.

problems.verificationNotes: Re-verified on 2026-09-20 against http://aimpl.org/hereddiscrep/1/ and the arXiv abstracts of the cited papers. Corrections made on 2026-09-20 following the comment by Richard Peng: added Potukuchi (arXiv:1811.01491) with the exact regimes $m = n$, $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$ (model $\mathcal{H}_1$) and $p = 1/2$, $n = \Omega(m \log m)$ (model $\mathcal{H}_2$); corrected the attribution of arXiv:1810.03374 to Bansal and Meka; distinguished bounds on discrepancy from bounds on hereditary discrepancy (Ezra-Lovett's bounds are hereditary, the later $O(\sqrt{t})$ bounds are stated for the discrepancy of the sampled system). The AimPL statement uses $m$ for the number of sets and $n$ for the number of elements, which this record follows. Status set to solved on 2026-09-20 on the basis of arXiv:2609.11189 (Guo-Fang-Lu, Corollary 1.2, a deterministic worst-case bound that applies to every realization of the random model and to every column-restriction); the paper is a preprint and its argument is existential.
problems.statusDetails: Solved in September 2026 by the worst-case Beck-Fiala theorem of Guo, Fang and Lu (arXiv:2609.11189, Corollary 1.2): every $t$-column-sparse $0/1$ matrix has $\mathrm{disc} < 3\sqrt{2\pi t}$, hence $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t})$ for the random system in every regime of $n, m, t$ (existentially). Earlier, random-model results: Ezra and Lovett (2015): $\mathrm{herdisc} = O(\sqrt{t \log t})$ w.h.p. for $m \geq n$ and $O(1)$ for $n \gg m^t$. Potukuchi (arXiv:1811.01491, 2018): $\mathrm{disc} = O(\sqrt{t})$ almost surely for $m = n$ and $\log^{10} n \ll t \ll \sqrt{n}$; also $\mathrm{disc} \leq 1$ in the i.i.d. $p = 1/2$ model when $n = \Omega(m \log m)$. Bansal and Meka (arXiv:1810.03374, 2019): tight $O(\sqrt{t})$ for all $n, m$ once $t = \Omega((\log\log m)^2)$. Franks-Saks (2020): $\mathrm{disc} \leq 2$ w.h.p. for $n = \Omega(m^3 \log^2 m)$; Hoberg-Rothvoss (2019): $\mathrm{disc} \leq 1$ w.h.p. in the Bernoulli model for $n \geq \Theta(m^2 \log m)$. Open: efficient algorithms for bounded $t$, and the exact order where the truth is $o(\sqrt{t})$.
